2.description: Interesting. Sea Elves well known for their mutual relationship with these creatures. Scales too small for a full-grown beast. Perhaps a crecheling. So, immature beasts that do not make it to adulthood still prove useful to the clans that rear them.

3.name: Verita Numida
3.description: That seems spot on. Detailed examination of the interior showed it once held several types of messages. Parchment, leather, I even found a type of powdered stone. Iâve heard of cultures using chiseled stone rods to carry shorthand letters, but I had no idea Sea Elf navies used them as well.

1.name: Amalien
1.description: Iâve never quite seen Dwemer cogs quite like this before. Weâve seen examples of constructs in unique environments, to be sure. Volcanic, submerged, at mountain tops, even reports of a ruin splintered in time. But these speak to a wholly unique type of tonal infrastructure.

2.name: Tuindoril
2.description: Iâd know these anywhere. Tonal remnants from the Xirkn-Zel ruins off the Gold Coast. While these still resemble cogs, Iâve found the coral has somehow replaced much of the brass. Whether an intentional process or a side-effect of long abandonment is unclear.

3.name: Tuindoril
3.description: A fascinating follow-up note. Despite these antiquities being more coral than brass, exposure to the harmonic frequencies we use for construct testing elicited a significant reaction, and attempted to turn! As if the cogs still remembered their purpose after all these years.

1.name: Ugron gro-Thumog
1.description: Hideous. But clearly a compass. Made of a pale, sickly coral and tarnished silver. Within is a sealed vessel filled with a cloudy and distasteful liquid. The directional needle is formed from a carved soul gem. It spins, regularly and consistently. But it does not align with north.

2.name: Muzah-Tei
2.description: Had the opportunity to test function while traveling. Needle aligns regularly and consistently. But locus of alignment shifts, like the stirring of a tide. Additional and distressing note to add to our records: carrying it overland caused me to hear whispers from unseen spirits.

3.name: Ugron gro-Thumog
3.description: I can now attest to this abominationâs function. It is a compass that aligns towards death. A necromancer-adventurer I met at a tavern aided me in some simple testing. I detest this thing. Codex closed.

1.name: Verita Numida
1.description: I have dined with members of the Imperial Elder Council and Iâm not sure Iâve ever seen such an ostentatious display of needless pompery. This chart is made of treated sea-silks! Every detail is made up of pearls of varying sizes, the largest of which is no bigger than a fingernail.

2.name: Reginus Buca
2.description: Ostentatious, yes, but made with an eye towards function as well. These pearls at first seem to outline nothing. But exploratory tests show that sea water splashed against the chart shift them to form coastlines and passable seaways. Ingenious!

3.name: Verita Numida
3.description: The depth of knowledge the Sea Elves have imbued in this artifact is astonishing. Unfortunately, other than identifying what appears to be a sea serpent breeding ground off the coast of Summerset, we lack the knowledge and understanding to fully understand what lies within.

1.name: Amalien
1.description: I was well into my initial examination when I realized what this is. Imagine my surprise! And, Iâve learned, this is a first for artifacts recovered from Dwemer constructs. Reginus laughed at me when I said Iâd learned something new about micro-etched tonal notation today and I had to admit where.

2.name: Tuindoril
2.description: I absolutely thought I was being hazed when I read the description of what Iâd been sent from Solitude. And yet, though this is a vessel without dignity it is chock full of meaning. Close examination reveals pipes once connected its interior to a larger system. Tonal calibration or sanitation?

3.name: Tuindoril
3.description: The Dwemer created for the love of the act itself. As best I can tell this artifact literally blurred the line between the mechanical and the deeply personal. Fascinating to think that in their hands even a simple chamberpot may have been part of an equation we canât fully understand.

1.name: Muzah-Tei
1.description: Supremely curious artifact. Residue of alchemical agents in the reservoir, delicate rune spirals all around the surface of the vessel. Interior compartments, all equal size. Never considered I would see such a thing in person: this is a caretaking vessel for immature Sload.

2.name: Muzah-Tei
2.description: Legend holds that Sloadlings left to fend for themselves. Some reports from All Flags Navy spoke of cultivated Sload broods. This vessel represents a cycle without compassion. Intervention, but not mercy. Accelerates development of best juveniles, prunes the weak, feeds the strong.

3.name: Muzah-Tei
3.description: Incredible to see this firsthand. And disturbing. Magical analysis hints at related vessels. Similar. But larger. With compartments that could accommodate people. Why? Disgusting and intriguing in equal measure.

1.name: Verita Numida
1.description: A sea-tossed cache of coins from every era! It appears to be a kind of trophy collection, and with the sea serpent sigil proudly displayed on the exterior Iâd hazard to guess some Sea Elf admiral was the past owner of this particular treasure.

2.name: Verita Numida
2.description: Even just as a historical exploration of coinage across the centuries this find is incredible! Iâve found hammered discs from pre-diaspora Summerset, trade tokens from the fall of the Wild Elf cities, even what I think is a Dwemer barter chit!

3.name: Tuindoril
3.description: We see long-term treasures like this come up from wrecks along the Gold Coast every once in a great while. The long lives of Maormer privateers means some of the sailors most loyal to King Orgnum have amassed vast treasure hordes. Incredible.

1.name: Tuindoril
1.description: A totem of pure horror, carved of pale driftwood and studded with fragments of shell, bone, and scales. At a glance it looks like a coiled tangle of serpents, but every ropy body refuses to resolve into a snake. Instead, this totem looks like a nest of swollen parasites all clinging one to the other.

2.name: Tuindoril
2.description: At the heart of the totem lay a hollowed-out cavity containing the desiccated shell of a louse broodmother, ritually positioned such that its many legs were splayed and fused to the wooden shell. A truly hideous sight.

3.name: Tuindoril
3.description: The interior surface of the totem was endlessly carved with mad whorls. Dense, spiraling grooves that danced when examined. Listening close to the totem, you could hear something. Not a sound exactly, but a pressure. A presence. Chilling.

1.name: Amalien
1.description: When I realized what this was, I called in everyone I could to collaborate. This is the remnant of an Animunculi schematic for an underwater beast. Almost artful in design, whereas most constructs are built with a kind of brutal simplicity.

2.name: Muzah-Tei
2.description: From long cross-discipline discussion, believe this was meant to imitate a tentacled underwater beast. A Dwemer octopus. Large, impossible, brass creation. Verita thinks they never quite got the articulation right.

3.name: Reginus Buca
3.description: As Iâve said to my colleagues, I think we are getting ahead of ourselves a bit here. The damage done to this schematic, which Tuindoril feels certain originated at the underwater Xirkn-Zel site, is extensive. Hard to tell anything for certain.

1.name: Tuindoril
1.description: A testament to the might of Tamriel sailing as one. This once-beautiful device is made of sturdy metals, carved with runes, and studded with soul gems. Beautiful, and designed to perfectly navigate the treacherous waters around Thras.

2.name: Amalien
2.description: Some rare texts from Archmage Syrabane describe how these navigational aides, scattered across the fleet, ensured even the worst of magical assaults wouldnât break formation. A way to mystically force a heading, when no others could be trusted.

3.name: Tuindoril
3.description: The casing here also bears the passing marks of sailors from across the continent. High Elven constellation glyphs. Colovian notations. And a set of notches by Redguard sailors. The greatest coalition to sail the seas, indeed. Inspiring!
